old: Confusing particle velocity with wave velocity: maximum particle speed is $a\omega$, while wave speed is $\omega/k$, and they are unrelated in general.
new: Confusing particle velocity with wave velocity: maximum particle speed is $a\omega$, while wave speed is $\omega/k$. These are different quantities, linked by $v_p = -v\,\partial y/\partial x$, so $v_{p,max}/v = ak$ (the maximum slope of the wave).
fixes: Particle velocity and wave speed are related, not 'unrelated'

old: Principle of superposition: when two or more waves overlap, the resultant displacement at any point is the algebraic (vector) sum of the individual displacements, $y = y_1+y_2$. Each wave then continues unaffected. For two waves of the same frequency with amplitudes $a_1$ and $a_2$ and phase difference $\phi$, the resultant amplitude is $A = \sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2+2a_1a_2\cos\phi$. Constructive interference occurs at $\phi = 2n\pi$, giving $A = a_1+a_2$. Destructive interference occurs at $\phi = (2n+1)\pi$, giving $A = |a_1-a_2|$. On reflection from a rigid boundary (fixed end, or a denser medium), the wave suffers a phase change of $\pi$, so the pulse is inverted. On reflection from a free end (rarer medium), there is no phase change. Frequency never changes on reflection. The reflected wave from a rigid end can be written $y_r = -a\sin(kx+\omega t)$.
new: Principle of superposition: when two or more waves overlap, the resultant displacement at any point is the algebraic (vector) sum of the individual displacements, $y = y_1+y_2$. Each wave then continues unaffected. For two waves of the same frequency with amplitudes $a_1$ and $a_2$ and phase difference $\phi$, the resultant amplitude is $A = \sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2+2a_1a_2\cos\phi$. Constructive interference occurs at $\phi = 2n\pi$, giving $A = a_1+a_2$. Destructive interference occurs at $\phi = (2n+1)\pi$, giving $A = |a_1-a_2|$. On reflection from a rigid boundary (fixed end, or a denser medium), the wave suffers a phase change of $\pi$, so the pulse is inverted. On reflection from a free end (rarer medium), there is no phase change. Frequency never changes on reflection. For an incident wave $y_i = a\sin(kx-\omega t)$ reflected at a rigid end at x = 0, the reflected wave is $y_r = a\sin(kx+\omega t)$, so that $y_i + y_r = 2a\sin kx\cos\omega t$ with a node at x = 0. NCERT writes $y_r = a\sin(kx+\omega t+\pi)$ only to illustrate the $\pi$ phase change.
fixes: Reflected wave at rigid end: state incident wave, use $y_r = a\sin(kx+\omega t)$ consistent with standing-wave form
